page: Amazon Web Services x8g.2xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance powered by the ARM64-based AWS Graviton processor family. It features 8 dedicated physical cores utilizing the AWS Neoverse-V2 model running at 2.8 GHz, with a 1.0 thread-per-core configuration. The processor includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of L3 cache. This instance is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 16.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and operates on a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong memory performance, with the Passmark memory score ranking in the top tier (top 10%). Single-threaded bzip3 decompression and Geekbench text processing also demonstrate strong performance, placing in the top 25%. However, CPU encryption capabilities are relatively weak, falling into the bottom 25% on the Passmark encryption test, which correlates with the absence of advanced vector extensions and specialized cryptographic flags like vaes. Large-block memory read bandwidth reaches 154.74 GB/sec, while write bandwidth is measured at 77.0 GB/sec.

The instance exhibits average performance across general compute metrics, including stress-ng multi-core CPU tests and Geekbench software compilation. Large language model inference speeds are a notable limitation, with prompt processing for medium-sized models scoring in the bottom 10%. Given the high memory density and strong memory bandwidth, the x8g.2xlarge is qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-bound workloads that do not require local NVMe storage or heavy cryptographic acceleration. It is highly suited for in-memory databases, caching layers, and memory-intensive data processing tasks.
